discovery: Experimental discovery of the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect (zero-field fractional Chern insulators) in moiré and rhombohedral graphene materials

nominees.name: Long Ju
nominees.affiliation: Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: topological quantum matter
motivation: For decades, fractionally charged anyons were thought to require Landau levels in strong magnetic fields. Theory predicted that topological flat Chern bands could host fractional quantum Hall physics without any field: the fractional Chern insulator. In 2023-2024 the nominees realised this idea. Xu's group observed fractional quantum anomalous Hall transport in twisted MoTe2, and Mak's group gave independent thermodynamic evidence in the same system. Ju's group found integer and fractional anomalous Hall plateaus in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene on hBN. Together these experiments establish, on two very different material platforms, that spontaneous time-reversal breaking together with band topology can produce fractionalized topological order at zero field. The work turns an abstract concept, band Chern numbers plus interactions, into tunable real materials. It has opened a fast-growing field that explores non-Abelian states, composite Fermi liquids and new routes to topological quantum computation.
